name: Reverse-osmosis water reuse train (NEWater-style)
principle: Follows the published advanced-purification (NEWater-style) train with licensor membrane equipment: secondary effluent passes microfiltration/ultrafiltration (licensor: Suez ZeeWeed / DuPont), then cartridge filtration, then reverse osmosis at high pressure (DuPont FilmTec / Hydranautics elements), then UV disinfection/advanced oxidation and mineralisation. The RO stage rejects salts, organics, pathogens and trace contaminants; UV destroys trace organics and provides a second pathogen barrier; conditioning restores hardness and pH for distribution.

process_steps.name: Reverse osmosis
equipment: FilmTec / Hydranautics spiral-wound elements in pressure vessels

performance.metric: RO permeate recovery in reuse trains
performance.basis: typical municipal reuse RO design recovery

performance.metric: log removal of pathogens across full train
performance.basis: multi-barrier claim of advanced purification schemes

sources.note: DuPont Water Solutions site (FilmTec RO/NF families), read 2026-11-13

costs.metric: installed capital cost, potable reuse train (MF/RO/UVAOP)
costs.basis: 20 mgd train, secondary-effluent feed with ocean disposal of concentrate: $120M capital = $6.00/gpd (~1,585 USD per m3/d). O&M $5.9M/yr separately; a 5 mgd train costs $52M.

source.note: Schimmoller & Kealy, The Cost of Overtreating Reclaimed Water, WateReuse webcast (2013): MF/RO/UVAOP train, 20 mgd, 2013 USD, read 2026-11-16
